\n <div><h2>Итог цикла</h2>\n:
Net result of the cycle

Acetyl-CoA + 3 NAD⁺ + FAD + GDP + Pi + 2 H₂O → 2 CO₂ + 3 NADH + FADH₂ + GTP + HS-CoA.

Eight hydrogen atoms (4 pairs) go to the respiratory chain and end up as water, and their energy ends up in ATP. The cycle itself does not use oxygen, but without oxygen it stops: NAD⁺ and FAD are not regenerated.

The cycle as a crossroads

The cycle is amphibolic: its intermediates are drawn off for synthesis (citrate → fatty acids and cholesterol, α-ketoglutarate → glutamate, succinyl-CoA → heme, oxaloacetate → aspartate and glucose). Losses are replenished by anaplerotic reactions, chiefly pyruvate carboxylase (with biotin): pyruvate + CO₂ → oxaloacetate.

Energy

Using textbook values (P/O = 3 for NADH and 2 for FADH₂), oxidation of 1 acetyl-CoA yields 12 ATP, and of glucose 38 ATP. Modern measurements give ≈ 2.5 and 1.5 ATP — that is, about 10 ATP per turn and 30–32 per glucose.

<b>Ротенон</b> (яд из корней тропических: Rotenone (a poison from the roots of tropical plants, used as an insecticide) and barbiturates block complex I. NADH is no longer oxidized, but the route from succinate through complex II still works — switch the substrate to succinate.

Yet (in cyanide poisoning) there is plenty of oxygen in the blood: the cells simply cannot use it; carbon monoxide also displaces oxygen from hemoglobin.
<b>Олигомицин</b> закупоривает протонный: Oligomycin plugs the proton channel of ATP synthase. Protons pile up outside, the gradient reaches its maximum — and respiration comes to a halt by itself: the chain cannot pump protons against an excessively steep gradient. This is respiratory control — respiration proceeds only when ATP is being used.

This is how newborns and hibernating animals keep warm; DNP was once sold “for weight loss” — people died of overheating.

It contains hemes a and a₃ and copper ions. It is the target of cyanide and CO.
<b>АТФ-синтаза (F₀F₁)</b> — настоящий ро: ATP synthase (F₀F₁) is a true rotary motor. Protons enter through subunit a (light blue), bind to the ring of c subunits (purple) and, turning it, exit into the matrix. The ring spins the γ shaft inside the F₁ head (α₃β₃): each of the three β subunits (gold) in turn binds ADP and Pi, squeezes them into ATP and releases it. Up to 100 revolutions per second; ≈3 protons per ATP (+1 to bring phosphate in).
<b>Тканевое дыхание.</b> Водород, снятый: Tissue respiration. Hydrogen removed from fuel as NADH and FADH₂ is passed along a chain of carriers embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane, from a more “negative” redox potential to a more “positive” one — to oxygen. The energy of the electrons (light blue) is used to pump protons (pink) out of the matrix. The result is a “dam” — the proton gradient (P. Mitchell’s chemiosmotic theory, Nobel Prize 1978). Protons flow back through ATP synthase and spin its rotor — this is how ATP is made. Click a complex or turn on a poison.

\n <div><h2>Окислительное фосфорили:
Oxidative phosphorylation

Carriers of the chain: NAD-dependent dehydrogenases (vitamin B3, niacin), flavoproteins with FMN and FAD (B2), iron–sulfur proteins, mobile ubiquinone (CoQ) — the hydrogen collector within the membrane, and cytochromes b, c₁, c, a, a₃ — heme proteins that carry electrons only. They are arranged in order of increasing redox potential: from NAD⁺/NADH (−0.32 V) to O₂/H₂O (+0.82 V).

Coupling of respiration to phosphorylation is provided by the proton gradient (ΔpH + membrane potential ≈ 0.2 V). The P/O ratio is the number of ATP formed per oxygen atom: 3 for NADH and 2 for FADH₂ in textbooks, ≈ 2.5 and 1.5 by current data.

Routes of oxygen consumption

~90% of O₂ goes to the respiratory chain. The rest goes to monooxygenases (liver cytochrome P450), oxidases and, unfortunately, electron leakage that forms reactive oxygen species (superoxide, H₂O₂), which are neutralized by superoxide dismutase, catalase and glutathione peroxidase.

<b>Оксидазный путь (~90% O₂).</b> Цитохр: Oxidase pathway (~90% of O₂). Cytochrome oxidase — the last complex of the respiratory chain — transfers 4 electrons and 4 protons to oxygen: O₂ + 4e⁻ + 4H⁺ → 2H₂O, holding the intermediate forms of oxygen in its active site — so no radicals escape. The energy goes into ATP synthesis.
<b>Оксигеназный путь.</b> <b>Монооксиген: Oxygenase pathway. Monooxygenases (cytochrome P450 of the liver and adrenal glands) insert one oxygen atom into a substrate, while the other goes to water: RH + O₂ + NADPH + H⁺ → ROH + H₂O + NADP⁺. This is how drugs and toxins are detoxified and how steroid hormones, bile acids and active vitamin D are synthesized. Dioxygenases insert both atoms (for example, in tryptophan breakdown and prostaglandin synthesis).
<b>Оксидазы с образованием пероксида.</b: Peroxide-forming oxidases. Flavin oxidases (amino acid oxidase, xanthine oxidase, monoamine oxidase) transfer 2 electrons to O₂, producing H₂O₂. In peroxisomes it is immediately broken down by catalase. H₂O₂ can also be useful: the thyroid gland (with its own NADPH oxidase, DUOX) uses it so that thyroid peroxidase can iodinate thyroglobulin.
<b>Свободнорадикальный путь (1–3% O₂).</: Free-radical pathway (1–3% of O₂). If oxygen receives a single electron (leakage from complexes I and III of the respiratory chain, NADPH oxidase), the superoxide anion O₂•⁻ forms — a particle with an unpaired electron. From it arise H₂O₂ and the most aggressive of all, the hydroxyl radical •OH. These are what we call reactive oxygen species (ROS).
Oxygen is the cell’s main oxidant. Almost all O₂ is turned into water in the mitochondria, but a small part takes other routes: it is inserted into molecules (oxygenases), converted into hydrogen peroxide (oxidases) or — one electron at a time — into free radicals. The thickness of the arrows and the bars show the proportions. Click a pathway.
<b>Активные формы кислорода и защита от: Reactive oxygen species and the defenses against them. SOD converts superoxide O₂•⁻ into H₂O₂; catalase and glutathione peroxidase (selenium, glutathione) convert H₂O₂ into water. With an Fe²⁺ ion, H₂O₂ gives •OH (the Fenton reaction), which triggers chain lipid peroxidation in the membrane (product: malondialdehyde). Vitamin E breaks the chain, and vitamin C regenerates vitamin E. Switch off defenses and add stress.
<b>Радикалы как оружие.</b> Нейтрофилы и: Radicals as weapons. Neutrophils and macrophages kill engulfed microbes with an “oxidative burst”: NADPH oxidase in the phagosome membrane (orange) produces superoxide, which gives rise to H₂O₂, and myeloperoxidase (green granules) makes hypochlorous acid HOCl — the active ingredient of chlorine bleach — from H₂O₂ and chloride. Click “Engulf a bacterium”.
<b>Фагоцитоз и респираторный взрыв.</b>: Phagocytosis and the respiratory burst. Bacteria are surrounded by membrane and end up in a phagosome. The cell’s oxygen consumption rises 50–100-fold — not for respiration, but to produce ROS. Superoxide, H₂O₂ and HOCl destroy bacterial membranes and proteins.
<b>Хроническая гранулематозная болезнь</: Chronic granulomatous disease is an inherited defect of NADPH oxidase. Phagocytes engulf bacteria but cannot kill them: there is no burst, and the microbes survive inside the cells. Patients suffer severe recurrent infections from childhood.
<b>Без супероксиддисмутазы</b> суперокси: Without superoxide dismutase superoxide accumulates. Mice lacking mitochondrial SOD (MnSOD) die soon after birth; mutations in Cu/Zn-SOD are one of the inherited causes of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (and the harm comes less from lost activity than from the toxicity of the altered protein).
<b>Без каталазы и глутатионпероксидазы</: Without catalase and glutathione peroxidase H₂O₂ builds up and, with iron, turns into •OH. Glutathione peroxidase needs selenium, and glutathione is regenerated with the help of NADPH from the pentose phosphate pathway — which is why in glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency red blood cells are destroyed by oxidative stress (for example, after eating fava beans or taking certain drugs).
<b>Без витамина E</b> некому обрывать це: Without vitamin E nothing breaks the chain: one lipid radical takes a hydrogen from its neighbor, that one from the next, and the damage spreads across the membrane.
<b>Без витамина C</b> окисленный витамин: Without vitamin C oxidized vitamin E (the tocopheroxyl radical) is not regenerated — the membrane’s defense is quickly exhausted.
Кислород даёт клетке энергию, но один не: Oxygen gives the cell energy, but a single unpaired electron turns it into a radical that can destroy membranes, proteins and DNA. The cell has a whole defense system against this.
\n <div><h2>Активные формы кислород:
Reactive oxygen species

Superoxide O₂•⁻, hydrogen peroxide H₂O₂, the hydroxyl radical •OH, singlet oxygen, as well as nitric oxide NO• and peroxynitrite. •OH lives for nanoseconds and reacts with the first molecule it meets — so there is no dedicated enzyme against it; the only defense is preventing its formation.

What they damage

Lipids — chain peroxidation of unsaturated fatty acids (membranes lose their integrity, malondialdehyde cross-links proteins). Proteins — oxidation of SH groups and amino acid residues. DNA — oxidation of bases (8-oxoguanine), strand breaks.

Defenses

  • Enzymes: SOD (Cu, Zn, Mn), catalase (Fe), glutathione peroxidase (Se), glutathione reductase (NADPH).
  • Non-enzymatic antioxidants: vitamins E and C, carotenoids, glutathione, uric acid, bilirubin, ceruloplasmin and transferrin (bind metal ions).

Benefits

ROS are weapons of phagocytes, signaling molecules (H₂O₂ regulates phosphatases) and participants in thyroid hormone synthesis. Harm arises from imbalance — oxidative stress: inflammation, ischemia and reperfusion, radiation, smoking, diabetes, aging.

Simplifications

  • Kinetics are qualitative; rates and concentrations are arbitrary.
  • Enzymes are shown as blobs; molecules are built from their chemical formulas.
  • Superoxide and hydroxyl are drawn as atoms with a halo.

\n <div><h2>Пути глюкозы</h2>\n:
Pathways of glucose

The dichotomous pathway (glycolysis): glucose → 2 pyruvate. Without oxygen — 2 lactate and 2 ATP; with oxygen — CO₂ and H₂O, 38 ATP (textbook value). The apotomic pathway (pentose phosphate) is direct oxidation producing NADPH and pentoses.

Three reactions are irreversible: the hexokinase (1), phosphofructokinase (3) and pyruvate kinase (10) reactions. Their enzymes are regulatory, and in gluconeogenesis they are replaced by bypass enzymes (I–IV).

Cori cycle

During intense work, muscle releases lactate into the blood; the liver turns it back into glucose and returns it to the muscle. The liver gets the energy for this (6 ATP) from fat oxidation.

Other sugars

Fructose and galactose enter glycolysis via their own enzymes. Inherited galactosemia (a defect of galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase) causes cataracts and liver and brain damage in infants; it is treated with a milk-free diet.

After a meal, glucose in the liver and muscles is converted to glucose-6-phosphate → glucose-1-phosphate → UDP-glucose (the activated form, green sparks). Glycogen synthase attaches residues to the ends of chains with α-1,4 bonds, and the branching enzyme transfers pieces of 6–7 residues, creating α-1,6 branch points (roughly every 8–12 residues). Glycogen phosphorylase (coenzyme pyridoxal phosphate, vitamin B6) cleaves glucose from the chain ends using phosphate rather than water, giving glucose-1-phosphate directly (the flying molecules) without spending ATP. Phosphorylase stops 4 residues short of a branch point; from there the debranching enzyme takes over. Breakdown is switched on by epinephrine (adrenaline; muscle, liver) and glucagon (liver) via cAMP and protein kinase A. In the liver glucose-6-phosphatase releases glucose into the blood; in muscle it goes only to the muscle’s own glycolysis.
<b>Сахар крови</b> держится в узком кори: Blood sugar is kept within a narrow fasting range of 3.3–5.5 mmol/L. After a meal glucose rises → insulin (light blue stream from the pancreatic β cells) makes the liver and muscles take up glucose and store it as glycogen and fat. During fasting sugar falls → glucagon (orange) makes the liver break down glycogen and synthesize glucose. The brain consumes ~120 g of glucose a day. Click “Eat” and compare with diabetes.
<b>Сахарный диабет 1 типа</b> — иммуните: Type 1 diabetes mellitus — the immune system has destroyed the β cells, and there is no insulin. Glucose cannot enter muscle and fat, while the liver keeps releasing it (glucagon is high). Sugar above the renal threshold (~10 mmol/L) spills into the urine (glucosuria), and fats are broken down to ketone bodies (ketoacidosis). Treatment: insulin.
<b>Сахарный диабет 2 типа</b> — инсулин: Type 2 diabetes mellitus — insulin is present, but the tissues respond poorly to it (insulin resistance, more common with obesity). Blood sugar falls slowly after a meal. Treatment: diet, exercise, metformin and other drugs.
Глюкоза — быстрое топливо, но хранить её: Glucose is a fast fuel, but it cannot be stored in free form: water would rush into the cell. So the liver and muscles store it in branched glycogen granules.
\n <div><h2>Запасы</h2>\n <p:
Stores

The liver holds about 100–120 g of glycogen (up to 6% of its mass); it lasts for 12–24 hours of fasting and serves the whole body. Muscles hold 300–400 g (1–2%), but only “for themselves”: muscle lacks glucose-6-phosphatase.

Regulation

Insulin activates glycogen synthase and inhibits phosphorylase (via phosphatases). Glucagon (liver) and epinephrine (liver and muscle) trigger a cascade: receptor → G protein → adenylate cyclase → cAMP → protein kinase A → phosphorylase kinase → phosphorylase. Phosphorylation switches phosphorylase on and at the same time switches glycogen synthase off. In muscle, breakdown is also accelerated by the Ca²⁺ of contraction and by AMP.

Glycogen storage diseases

Inherited defects of the breakdown enzymes: von Gierke disease (glucose-6-phosphatase — hypoglycemia, enlarged liver), Pompe disease (lysosomal α-glucosidase — heart involvement), McArdle disease (muscle phosphorylase — cramps during exercise). Aglycogenoses are defects of synthesis.

Models

  • The granule is simplified: a few hundred residues out of ~30,000; each bead is one glucose residue.
  • The blood sugar model is qualitative: “8 hours” are compressed into half a minute.

<b>Переваривание углеводов.</b> Крахмал: Carbohydrate digestion. Starch (chains of glucose) is first cut by salivary amylase, but the main work is done by pancreatic amylase (light blue drops), yielding maltose and short fragments. Disaccharides are split by brush border enzymes on the microvilli: maltase, sucrase-isomaltase (sucrose → glucose + fructose) and lactase (lactose → galactose + glucose). Glucose and galactose enter the cell together with Na⁺ via SGLT1 (light blue transporters), fructose via GLUT5 (orange), and all of them exit into the blood via GLUT2 (purple). Fiber (cellulose) is not digested: humans lack enzymes that cleave the β-1,4 bonds between glucose residues (cellulases).
<b>Лактазная недостаточность.</b> У боль: Lactase deficiency. In most adults worldwide, lactase activity declines after weaning (among Northern Europeans it more often persists — a mutation that spread together with dairy farming). Undigested lactose passes into the colon: it holds water (osmotic diarrhea), and bacteria ferment it into gases (H₂, CO₂, methane) and acids — bloating and pain. Fermented dairy products, lactose-free milk and lactase tablets help.
<b>Галактоза и фруктоза в печени</b> пре: Galactose and fructose in the liver are converted into glucose metabolites. Galactose: galactokinase → galactose-1-phosphate → GALT (galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase) transfers a UMP group to it from UDP-glucose, giving UDP-galactose and glucose-1-phosphate; epimerase converts UDP-galactose back into UDP-glucose, closing the loop. Fructose: fructokinase → fructose-1-phosphate → aldolase B → dihydroxyacetone phosphate and glyceraldehyde (phosphorylated by triokinase) → glycolysis. Fructose bypasses the main regulatory step of glycolysis (phosphofructokinase), so an excess of it is rapidly converted into fat. Choose an enzyme defect.
<b>Галактоземия</b> (дефект ГАЛТ, ~1 : 5: Galactosemia (GALT defect, ~1 : 50,000). After the first milk feedings the infant develops vomiting, jaundice, an enlarged liver and hypoglycemia. Galactose-1-phosphate accumulates and is toxic to the liver, kidneys and brain; aldose reductase converts galactose into galactitol, which accumulates in the lens — cataract (the lens turns cloudy). Treatment: lifelong exclusion of milk and lactose; the disease is included in newborn screening.
<b>Дефект галактокиназы</b> — более мягк: Galactokinase deficiency is a milder form: galactose is not phosphorylated, builds up in the blood and is converted into galactitol; the main manifestation is cataract, and the liver is spared.
<b>Наследственная непереносимость фрукто: Hereditary fructose intolerance (aldolase B defect). Fructose-1-phosphate accumulates and “locks up” phosphate — ATP falls (the bar), and glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis are inhibited: sweets, fruit or honey are followed by severe hypoglycemia, vomiting, and liver and kidney damage. Children start avoiding sweets on their own. Treatment: exclude fructose, sucrose and sorbitol.
<b>Эссенциальная фруктозурия</b> (дефект: Essential fructosuria (fructokinase defect) is a harmless condition: fructose is not phosphorylated in the liver and is excreted in the urine; it is discovered by chance.
Хлеб, сахар и молоко превращаются в три: Bread, sugar and milk are turned into three simple sugars — glucose, fructose and galactose. How they cross the intestinal wall, and what happens when a single enzyme is missing.
\n <div><h2>Углеводы пищи</h2>\n:
Dietary carbohydrates

A person eats 300–400 g of carbohydrates a day: about 60% starch (bread, cereals, potatoes), about 30% sucrose, up to 10% lactose. Only monosaccharides are absorbed. Glucose and galactose enter the cell actively, together with Na⁺ (SGLT1) — which is why oral rehydration solutions contain both salt and glucose. Fructose is absorbed more slowly, by facilitated diffusion (GLUT5).

Enzymes

  • α-Amylase of saliva and pancreas — α-1,4 bonds of starch.
  • Isomaltase — α-1,6 bonds at branch points.
  • Sucrase, maltase, lactase — on the brush border membrane.

After absorption

All monosaccharides reach the liver via the portal vein. Galactose and fructose are almost completely converted in the liver into glucose, glycogen or fat.

  • Sugars are shown as icons: a hexagon for glucose and galactose, a pentagon for fructose.
  • The starch chain is shortened to a few residues, and time is compressed.

<b>Пальмитиновая кислота</b> (C16:0) — с: Palmitic acid (C16:0) is the most common saturated acid: palm oil, butter, meat. The body synthesizes it itself from acetyl-CoA. Its straight chain lets the molecules pack tightly, which is why saturated fats are solid at room temperature.
<b>Стеариновая кислота</b> (C18:0) — нас: Stearic acid (C18:0) is saturated; it is found in beef and mutton fat and in cocoa butter.
<b>Олеиновая кислота</b> (C18:1, ω-9) —: Oleic acid (C18:1, ω-9) is the main acid of olive oil. A single cis double bond creates a ~30° kink: the molecules do not pack tightly, so the oil is liquid and the membrane flexible.
<b>Элаидиновая кислота</b> — та же C18:1: Elaidic acid is the same C18:1 but with a trans double bond: the chain is straight, like a saturated one. Trans fats form during industrial hydrogenation of oils (margarines, deep-frying fats) and raise the risk of atherosclerosis — they are restricted by law.
<b>Линолевая кислота</b> (C18:2, ω-6) —: Linoleic acid (C18:2, ω-6) is essential: humans lack the enzymes that introduce a double bond beyond carbon 9. Sunflower and corn oil. Arachidonic acid is built from it.
<b>α-Линоленовая кислота</b> (C18:3, ω-3: α-Linolenic acid (C18:3, ω-3) is essential; flaxseed oil, walnuts. It is the precursor of the ω-3 acids of fish oil (EPA, DHA), which are important for the brain and retina.
<b>Арахидоновая кислота</b> (C20:4, ω-6): Arachidonic acid (C20:4, ω-6) is stored in membrane phospholipids. From it the enzymes cyclooxygenase and lipoxygenase make eicosanoids — prostaglandins, thromboxanes and leukotrienes (inflammation, pain, clotting). Aspirin and ibuprofen block cyclooxygenase.
<b>Триацилглицерины (нейтральные жиры)</: Triacylglycerols (neutral fats) are esters of glycerol and three fatty acids. They are the most compact form of energy storage: 1 g of fat yields 9 kcal versus 4 kcal for carbohydrates, and it binds no water. An adult carries 10–15 kg of fat — enough for a month of fasting.
<b>Глицерофосфолипиды</b> — дифильные мо: Glycerophospholipids are amphiphilic molecules: a hydrophilic “head” (phosphate + choline, ethanolamine or serine) and two hydrophobic “tails”. In water they spontaneously assemble into a bilayer — the basis of all membranes. Shown is a real phosphatidylcholine (lecithin) from the membrane model.
<b>Холестерин</b> — стероид с четырьмя к: Cholesterol is a steroid with four rings and an OH group. It inserts into membranes and regulates their fluidity; bile acids, steroid hormones and vitamin D are made from it. About 80% of cholesterol is synthesized by the body itself (mainly in the liver).
<b>Желчные кислоты</b> (холевая, хенодез: Bile acids (cholic, chenodeoxycholic) are synthesized in the liver from cholesterol. One side of the molecule is hydrophilic (three OH groups), the other hydrophobic: they emulsify fat, activate lipase and aid absorption. 90% return to the liver (enterohepatic circulation).
<b>Стероидные гормоны</b> (кортизол, аль: Steroid hormones (cortisol, aldosterone, sex hormones) are cholesterol derivatives synthesized by the adrenal glands and gonads. They cross the membrane and act on genes (see the “Hormones” section).
<b>Мембрана</b> — двойной слой фосфолипи: The membrane is a double layer of phospholipids. This is a real fragment from a molecular dynamics computer model: 128 phosphatidylcholine molecules, each atom a bead (● phosphorus, ● choline nitrogen, ● oxygen; beige — hydrocarbon tails). The heads face the water and the tails hide inside; the thickness is about 4 nm. Cholesterol (yellow) is embedded between the phospholipids, and an integral protein, rhodopsin (PDB 1U19), spans the whole membrane. The membrane is fluid: lipids travel micrometers in a second.
<b>Высшие жирные кислоты</b> — длинные у: Long-chain fatty acids are long hydrocarbon chains with a carboxyl group (on the left of the model — the red oxygen atoms). Saturated ones have no double bonds and are straight. Unsaturated ones contain double bonds; natural ones are in the cis form, with a kink. Click an acid.
<b>Классы липидов</b>: объединяет их нер: Lipid classes: what unites them is insolubility in water. Click a molecule.
<b>Переваривание жиров</b> идёт в тонкой: Fat digestion takes place in the small intestine. Bile acids (green) from the liver break a large fat droplet into small ones — they emulsify it, increasing the surface area thousands of times. Pancreatic lipase with colipase (pink) cleaves off fatty acids, leaving 2-monoacylglycerol. Together with bile acids the products form micelles and are absorbed by the villus cells; there TAGs are reassembled and packaged into chylomicrons, which enter the lymph rather than the blood. Without bile (a blocked duct) fat passes out in the stool — steatorrhea — and fat-soluble vitamins are lost.
Жиры — самый плотный запас энергии и осн: Fats are the densest energy store and the basis of all cell membranes. They share one trait: they don’t get along with water.
\n <div><h2>Липиды</h2>\n <p:
Lipids

Lipids are a diverse group of substances whose common property is hydrophobicity. The main classes: triacylglycerols (energy storage), glycerophospholipids and sphingolipids (membranes), steroids (cholesterol, bile acids, steroid hormones, vitamin D), fat-soluble vitamins and eicosanoids.

Functions: energy (fats provide up to 40% of energy), structural (membranes), regulatory (hormones, eicosanoids), protective and insulating (subcutaneous fat), and solvent for fat-soluble vitamins.

Conditions for digestion

Emulsified fat, active pancreatic lipase (pH 7.5–8), the protein colipase, bile acids. In adults, fats are barely digested in the stomach.
